quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When parked on the road, a motorcycle should:

options.text: Park at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees from the curb.
Park so no wheel or fender touches the curb.
Park parallel to the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees from the curb.
questions.explanation: A parked motorcycle should be at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees from the curb. At least one wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a potential problem?

options.text: A change in road surface ahead
Other traffic around you
Road conditions that stay the same as you approach

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions that stay the same as you approach
questions.explanation: Look ahead for potential problems on the road. Make a plan to reduce the risks they create.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Help you fit in with traffic flow.
Give you a way to escape if danger happens.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a way to escape if danger happens.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It also discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
It automatically brakes based on your riding style.
It applies the brake when you downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems that link the front and rear brakes together when you apply the rear brake pedal. Check your owner's manual to learn about your specific motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: If you need to react to a road hazard, do not:

options.text: Fail to let other drivers know you are there.
Change your speed as needed.
Use your horn, lights, or signals to alert others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fail to let other drivers know you are there.
questions.explanation: To create more space and stay safer, let other drivers know you are there. Use your horn, lights, and signals. Change your speed to fit the situation. Adjust your lane position or direction as needed.

questions.question: When traveling at night, you should:

options.text: Ride as fast as possible.
Ride at the maximum speed limit.
Ride slow enough to stop within your headlight's light.
Ride as fast as other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slow enough to stop within your headlight's light.
questions.explanation: At night, ride at a speed that lets you stop within the area lit by your headlight. Slow down when visibility is poor.

questions.question: A benefit of keeping space between you and other vehicles is that:

options.text: You can draft off other vehicles better.
You can stop faster.
You have more time to react to what other drivers do.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to react to what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your motorcycle at all times. This gives you time to react to hazards and space to maneuver safely.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You have time to react to hazards.
You have space to maneuver.
You have more time to speed up when entering a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to speed up when entering a curve.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your motorcycle at all times. This helps you react quickly and maneuver safely if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: Motorcycles may pass on the right:

options.text: If there is at least eight feet of clear pavement.
By riding on the road shoulder.
By riding on the grass if it is level.

questions.correctAnswerText: If there is at least eight feet of clear pavement.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right only if there is at least eight feet of clear pavement to the right of the vehicle you are passing. Never leave the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection:

options.text: Takes only a few minutes.
Takes about an hour.
Should only be done by a certified mechanic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Takes only a few minutes.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-ride inspection before every ride. It usually takes just a few minutes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Yield to other drivers.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle, you:

options.text: May exceed the speed limit by 10 mph.
Must not exceed the speed limit.
Are required to ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must not exceed the speed limit.
questions.explanation: You must obey the speed limit when passing. Only pass where it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle:

options.text: The mirrors provide a perfect view.
The mirrors do not show your blind spots.
The mirrors should not be used, except when parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: The mirrors do not show your blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots, just like car mirrors. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which factor does not greatly affect your blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: Age
The amount of alcohol consumed
Body weight

questions.correctAnswerText: Age
questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol content depends on how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Age does not greatly affect it.

questions.question: If bright sunlight makes it hard to see your motorcycle's turn signals, you should:

options.text: Continue to use the mechanical turn signals.
Honk your horn to tell drivers about upcoming turns.
Use hand signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use hand signals.
questions.explanation: Use hand signals when bright sunlight makes your turn signals hard to see. It is very important to clearly tell other drivers about your turns.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
No left turn
No U-turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When alcohol and drugs are used together, the effects:

options.text: Are less dangerous than when either is used alone.
Often cancel each other out.
Can be stronger than when either is used alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be stronger than when either is used alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can affect your ability to ride safely. Mixing drugs with alcohol makes the effects much worse.

questions.question: When other vehicles are slow or stopped:

options.text: A motorcyclist should not weave between lanes of traffic.
It is acceptable for a motorcyclist to weave in and out of traffic lanes.
A motorcyclist should ride in a straight line between two lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcyclist should not weave between lanes of traffic.
questions.explanation: Riding between stopped or slow-moving vehicles is dangerous. Vehicles may change lanes, doors may open, or arms may stick out. Motorcycles need the full width of a lane to stay safe.

questions.question: When braking on a motorcycle:

options.text: The rear brake should be applied first.
The front brake should be applied first.
The front and rear brakes should be applied at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear brakes should be applied at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Using only the rear brake may prevent you from developing the skill to use the front brake when you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic
Right lane ends
Merge

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that traffic is merging ahead.

questions.question: A "wobble" is when the front wheel and handlebars shake suddenly. What usually causes this?

options.text: Wrong tire pressure or uneven weight.
Front wheel not fastened tightly to the frame.
Hitting an object with the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wrong tire pressure or uneven weight.
questions.explanation: A wobble is when the front wheel and handlebars shake side to side. This usually happens because of wrong tire pressure, poor weight distribution, or bad accessories.

questions.question: Alcohol reaches the brain ________ being consumed.

options.text: Within minutes of
About an hour after
About two hours after

questions.correctAnswerText: Within minutes of
questions.explanation: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes of being consumed and starts to affect your riding ability. It is illegal and dangerous to operate a motorcycle while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: Compared to a car, a motorcycle needs _____ attention.

options.text: Less frequent
The same amount of
More frequent

questions.correctAnswerText: More frequent
questions.explanation: A motorcycle needs more frequent attention than a car. You must find any problems before riding in traffic or at highway speeds.

questions.question: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to:

options.text: Keep your headlight on.
Make eye contact with drivers.
Wave at drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times to help others see your motorcycle. Motorcycles made after 1978 turn on the headlight automatically when running. Check that your headlight works before every ride.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:

options.text: Use both brakes.
Use the front brake only.
Use the rear brake only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Using both brakes helps you stop quickly when you need to.
